thread:
SRE Bot: PAGER: Accelerator capacity alert for pool 'prod-accel-pool' — queue length 3200, GPU saturation 95%, autoscaler attempted scale but hit pool limit=40. Paging on-call SRE.
Alex W: on it. seeing queue growth, dashboard looks nasty.
Priya K: FYI I'm seeing lots of cuda/xid and OOMs in driver logs for nodes in zone-a. Could be reducing effective capacity.
Alex W: OK. quick triage: does autoscaler reject because of cloud quota or internal policy? @Diego R can you check quota side?
Diego R: checking provider quotas now. also looking at scheduler errors.
Marta L: seeing repeated node flaps around 15:02-15:05 UTC, docker daemon restarts and driver reloads. probable kernel-driver interaction.
Alex W: start mitigations: 1) throttle new low-priority requests at the edge; 2) divert heavy model variants to fallback smaller models; 3) cordon any nodes with repeated Xid logs.
Priya K: applied rate-limit rule for route /v1/generate - 30% reduction for non-critical keys. added temporary routing to model 'redwood-small-v1' for Horde customers.
SRE Bot: Incident note created: INC-2026-0315-accel-exhaust. Severity: Sev2.
Diego R: cloud quota looks OK — we have free GPUs in other AZs but autoscaler is refusing due to node provisioning errors: 'instance creation failed: driver-init-timeout'.
Alex W: that matches kernel/driver failures preventing new instances from registering. can infra try spinning nodes with older kernel/driver?
Marta L: we have a handful of nodes with kernel 5.15 that are stable. current problematic ones run 6.2 + driver 540. I'll mark instances with 6.2 as suspect.
Priya K: log snippets below from one node:
```
[2026-03-15T15:02:43Z] runtime: cuda:xid=77 detected on device 0 - out of memory - process runtime_server(4821)
[2026-03-15T15:02:44Z] nvidia-driver: rmmod: module unloaded unexpectedly
[2026-03-15T15:03:01Z] kubelet: Node prod-accel-23 lost heartbeat, kube-proxy restarting, pods Evicted
```
Alex W: good logs. plan: quarantine flaky nodes, increase autoscaler max temporarily by requesting approval from infra-owner to bypass pool limit, and scale from other AZs.
Diego R: started provisioning 8 nodes in zone-b with kernel 5.15 + driver 535. will attach to pool if healthy.
Marta L: cordoning nodes with repeated Xid errors: prod-accel-12, prod-accel-23, prod-accel-17. Running `kubectl drain` now.
Alex W: command used:
```
kubectl cordon prod-accel-23
kubectl drain prod-accel-23 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --force
```
Priya K: after cordon/drain, immediate drop in OOM logs on remaining healthy nodes. queue still high but throughput resumed on fallback models.
Customer Success (Eve): pulling impacted customers list — looks like two Dedicated customers had degraded latency and increased 5xxs; Hosted customers got automated fallback to smaller model. CX outreach in progress.
Alex W: status update for on-call handoff: mitigation work in progress, autoscaler provisioning from zone-b started, quarantined nodes cordoned. Remaining tasks: confirm new nodes register and accept pods; monitor queue shrink; confirm no regression in driver logs.
Diego R: new nodes booted and joined cluster at 15:20 UTC, kubelet healthy, runtime-server up. attaching logs: no immediate Xid events so far.
Priya K: traffic to heavy model variants remains throttled. seeing drop in queue from 3.2k to ~1.1k after new nodes accepted, and latency for critical customers improving.
SRE Bot: NOTE: Autoscaler attempted 3 retries and recorded failures due to driver init error; now successful attach count +8.
Marta L: still seeing a residual memory spike on one host, investigating driver version mismatch with nightly build. will keep it cordoned.
Alex W: preparing handoff to next oncall in 30 mins. leaving playbook in channel, and adding runbook steps we executed to the incident doc.
Alex W: runbook snippet added:
```
- throttle non-critical routes at edge
- route heavy models to fallback small models
- cordon + drain nodes with Xid/OOM logs
- provision nodes with known-good kernel+driver
- monitor queue and rollback throttles when stable
```
Diego R: Quick note — autoscaler config changed: pool max temporarily bumped from 40 -> 60 with approval token. revert when stable.
Customer Success (Eve): Notifying customers A and B with timeline and mitigation steps. No data loss, degraded perf only.
Priya K: looks stable for now. driver OOMs stopped after quarantines. queue trending down to 300 and continuing.
Alex W: handoff to Diego R @ 16:30 UTC. Diego, you own until clear + postmortem. Leaving pager context and relevant logs in the incident doc. :white_check_mark:
Diego R: acknowledged, taking over. will open postmortem and schedule post-incident review with infra and runtime teams.
SRE Bot: Incident severity downgraded to Sev3 at 16:45 UTC. Monitoring for 2 hours.
Alex W: thanks team. follow-up actions: pin driver version for pool images, add guard in autoscaler to prefer AZ failover before hitting pool hard limit, and add more detailed Xid alerting thresholds.
Diego R: creating follow-up tickets and assigning owners.
Customer Success (Eve): customers notified, CS will follow up tomorrow for RCA.
Marta L: leaving final note — suspect nightly driver build introduced instability, will coordinate with runtime-release.
Diego R: end of handoff.
